evidence: src/domain/TaskStatus.ts: TASK_STATUSES, TaskStatus and isTaskStatus are the only definition of valid statuses. Task.ts and TaskRepository.ts (TaskFilter.status) import them instead of redefining them.
src/domain/errors.ts: DomainError with DomainErrorCode is the base for ValidationError, NotFoundError and TaskAlreadyDoneError. Project.ts, User.ts and Task.ts all throw these classes.
src/domain/Task.ts: Task.create checks status with isTaskStatus and markDone throws TaskAlreadyDoneError, so the module's own abstractions are used.
src/domain/ProjectRepository.ts, TaskRepository.ts, UserRepository.ts: all three port interfaces follow the same save/findById shape and are typed against the domain entities.
src/domain/Project.ts and src/domain/User.ts: each create() runs a similar name-trim check, but they are separate entity rules with different messages, not one duplicated invariant.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: This unit passes. All eight files belong to the task-management domain: entities, repository ports, a status value type, and the error types the domain uses. Each invariant is defined in one place. The list of valid task statuses lives only in TaskStatus.ts, and the other files reuse it. Every domain error is defined in errors.ts on the shared DomainError base. No file bypasses the module's own pieces: Task uses isTaskStatus and the error classes from errors.ts, and the repositories refer to the entity types. Project.create and User.create both trim and check a name in the same way. That is the same pattern applied to two different entities, with its own error message in each, so it is not a single rule duplicated across files. It is too minor to fail the unit.
